PM Decision Memo

The Command Center is the weekly PM decision layer above the source decks. Current stance is Underweight for equity beta under Cut Risk And Wait For Repair. Internal damage or weak trend participation argues for beta restraint. The priority is drawdown control until breadth repair is visible. ETF z-scores show 16 washed-out ETFs, so repair candidates matter more than chasing current winners. Breadth and ETF leadership set the opportunity set; financial conditions and rates/credit set the risk budget; S&P 500 drawdown risk sizes the downside being underwritten; CFTC positioning adjusts for crowding; and the full VAMS buy/sell universe plus fresh flips adjusts for momentum confirmation.

Leadership: XTN, IHF, IHE, PEJ Risk watch: GDXJ, SIL, BTC-USD, SILJ VAMS overlay: -7.4 Positioning overlay: +2.0 FCI overlay: -2.0 Regime: Cut Risk And Wait For Repair

PM read: start with beta, then choose sector/ETF leadership, then validate with financial conditions, rates/credit, positioning, and VAMS. Decision Rule

Use the agreement score as the compression layer across the eight live checks: risk appetite, breadth, ETF leadership/z-scores, rates/credit, financial conditions, drawdown risk, positioning, and VAMS. It is not a replacement for the evidence.

6-8 checksOwn confirmed risk; avoid only the extended/crowded pockets.
4-5 checksSelective exposure; group confirmation matters more than broad beta.
0-3 checksDefensive posture; wait for breadth, VAMS, FCI, or rates/credit repair.

What Would Change The View?

PathTriggerPM Action
Upgrade RiskAgreement score rises to 6-8 checks, FCI >55 or improving, drawdown risk falls below 45, 50/200DMA breadth expands, and VAMS fresh buys broaden beyond narrow leaders.Raise beta and add to confirmed group leaders.
Hold / SelectiveAgreement holds at 4-5 checks, FCI neutral, leadership remains concentrated, drawdown risk stays elevated but stable, and z-score extension stays elevated.Keep current stance; rotate inside leaders and avoid broad chase.
Downgrade RiskAgreement falls below 4 checks, FCI breaks below 45 or rolls over, drawdown risk rises above 60, damage breadth rises, and VAMS sells broaden.Cut beta, raise quality/cash, and wait for repair.

Validated Risk-Budget Evidence

This is the statistical proof layer for the aggregate gauge. It tests whether the master score separates lower-risk S&P 500 environments from higher-risk ones using future 6M max drawdown and future 6M >10% drawdown hit rates. How To Use It

This is the first-pass risk-temperature read before the detailed PM table. It does not replace group diagnostics; it tells you whether the broad tape is rewarding risk-taking, demanding selectivity, or warning that repair is needed.

75-100Risk-on: broad tape supports invested exposure; watch extension and crowding.
55-75Constructive: stay invested, but let group confirmation drive where to add.
45-55Neutral: use selectivity; avoid forcing broad beta without confirmation.
25-45Defensive: lower beta, favor quality, and wait for breadth repair.
0-25Stress: prioritize drawdown control and capital preservation.

How To Use It

This is the downside-underwriting layer. Risk appetite says whether the tape is rewarding risk; financial conditions say whether the macro backdrop is helping; drawdown risk says how much S&P 500 downside risk historically followed a similar setup.

75-100Stress: prioritize drawdown control and reduce broad beta unless hedged.
60-75High: stay selective, reduce chase risk, and favor confirmed/hedged exposure.
45-60Elevated: require cleaner breadth, VAMS, and FCI confirmation.
25-45Watch: risk is manageable but still monitored.
0-25Low: downside risk is not the primary constraint.

This is the model validation layer. It compares future drawdowns after low-risk readings against future drawdowns after high-risk readings. A useful signal should show deeper average/worst future drawdowns and higher 5%, 10%, and 15% drawdown hit rates in high-risk buckets.

The right side of the table is the forward drawdown test. Low-Risk / High-Risk Avg Max DD show average future max drawdown after low- versus high-risk readings. Extra Avg DD Risk is normalized so positive means high-risk readings led to deeper average drawdowns. Worst Max DD shows the worst forward drawdown in each bucket. The >5%, >10%, and >15% DD Hit columns show how often SPY later crossed those drawdown thresholds within the horizon. Extra 10% Hit Risk is also normalized so positive means high-risk readings had more frequent 10% drawdowns.

Methodology

This page defines the language used throughout the packet so the weekly read is explainable in a client or investment-committee setting.

Health Score

Composite breadth score from the individual ETF breadth metric files. It answers: are the holdings inside the ETF broadly confirming the price move?

35%Trend Breadth: average % of holdings above 20DMA, 50DMA, and 200DMA
20%Leadership Breadth: average % making new highs or sitting near 52-week highs
15%Positive 20D Return: % of holdings with positive 20-day return
20%Relative Strength: average % outperforming across 30D, 60D, 90D, 6M, and 1Y
-10%Damage Breadth: penalizes new lows and holdings more than 20% below 52-week highs

Weekly Change

Health 1W Change is the 5-trading-day change in the Health Score. This matters because a strong ETF with falling internal health is different from a strong ETF whose internals are still broadening.

ImproverHealth score rising over the last 5 trading days
DeterioratorHealth score falling over the last 5 trading days
ConfirmationPrice return and breadth health moving in the same direction
DivergencePrice return and breadth health moving in opposite directions

Price Proxy Health

For ETFs without constituent breadth files, the packet uses a technical proxy so group summaries are complete instead of blank. The proxy is intentionally less punitive after volatile single-day moves; drawdown damage begins once price is more than 10% below its trailing 1-year high.

45%Trend proxy: above 50DMA, above 200DMA, and positive 1M return
40%Leadership proxy: percentile rank of 1W, 1M, and 3M returns
15%Damage proxy: penalty for drawdown more than 10% below the trailing 1-year high
Health SourceTables mark each row as Breadth or Price proxy

Trend Breadth

Measures whether holdings are above key moving averages. This is the cleanest internal trend confirmation signal.

Above 20DMAShort-term trend participation
Above 50DMAIntermediate trend participation
Above 200DMALong-term trend participation

Damage Breadth

Measures internal stress. High damage breadth means the ETF price can look stable while many constituents remain impaired.

20D New LowsFresh short-term breakdowns
52W New LowsLong-term breakdowns
>20% Below HighDrawdown damage below the ETF surface

ETF Z-Score Overlay

Uses the ETF macro technical deck to judge whether leadership is extended versus each ETF's own history or whether weakness is becoming a repair candidate.

Extension ZAverage of available own-history return z-scores and 50DMA deviation z-score. High positive readings flag chase risk. Negative readings flag washed-out conditions.
MA Dev ZHow far the ETF sits from its moving-average trend versus its own historical behavior.
RS ZRelative-strength z-score versus SPY when available. This is the positive confirmation component.
Repair CandidateExtension Z at or below -0.75 plus either improving 1W breadth health or a positive 1W price return. This flags early repair, not full confirmation.
Z OverlayGroup-level score adjustment: RS z-score bonus minus extension/washout penalties, clipped from -8 to +8, then added to Strategy Score.
Decision UsePositive overlay supports allocation; negative overlay says leadership may be stretched or weakness still needs repair.

How Z-Scores Flow Through

The z-score layer is not just a table. It feeds the group Strategy Score, then flows into the Model Allocation and Allocation Playbook. Cross-Analysis and Regime also show it explicitly as the chase-versus-repair layer.

Cross-AnalysisAdds the question: are we chasing extended winners or buying confirmed repair?
RegimeShows average extension, extended ETF count, washed-out count, and average group z-score overlay.
Model AllocationUses Strategy Score after the z-score overlay is included.
Allocation PlaybookUses the same allocation table, so it stays consistent with the model.

Apex Risk Appetite Gauge

Aggregate 0-100 read built from the same ETF price universe used by the group allocation workflow. It is the broad tape input; the PM allocation tables then add breadth, VAMS, CFTC positioning, financial conditions, rates/credit, and z-score overlays.

25%% of ETFs above 50DMA
20%% of ETFs above 200DMA
20%% of ETFs with positive 1M returns
25%1M and 3M aggregate momentum percentiles
10%Drawdown relief percentile

Financial Conditions Ease Index

Macro risk-budget overlay built from USD, oil, 5Y yield, 10Y yield, VIX, and MOVE. Higher scores mean easier conditions. Each input is ranked versus its own rolling history and inverted where lower levels are easier.

65%Level Ease: current level percentile versus roughly the prior 3 years, inverted so lower volatility/rates/USD/oil score easier.
35%3M Easing Impulse: 3-month change percentile versus the same input's own history, inverted so falling pressure scores easier.
OverlayVery easy/easy conditions add to risk sleeves; tight/very tight conditions subtract from risk sleeves and raise the cash/quality bar.
Decision UseFCI does not replace breadth or VAMS. It decides how much risk budget to give confirmed signals.

S&P 500 Drawdown Risk Gauge

Downside-underwriting score where higher means higher future S&P 500 drawdown risk. It is separate from risk appetite: markets can be rewarding risk while drawdown risk is also elevated, which argues for smaller adds, better entry discipline, or hedges. The validation target is future max drawdown; forward returns are deliberately excluded because sharp recoveries can obscure the risk question.

30%Breadth Damage: weak 50/200DMA participation, weak 1M breadth, and broad ETF drawdown pressure.
20%Market Pressure: SPY 1M/3M momentum deterioration and drawdown from the 1Y high.
20%Financial Stress: VIX, MOVE, USD, oil, 5Y, and 10Y level/impulse stress percentiles.
15%Leadership Fragility: defensives outperforming cyclicals/growth and cap-weight leadership beating equal weight.
15%Credit / Rates Stress: HY/IG OAS level and impulse plus MOVE/rates pressure when rates-deck FRED cache is available; otherwise HYG/LQD versus SHY is used as the fallback proxy.
BacktestFor each historical score date, future SPY max drawdown is measured over 1M, 3M, 6M, and 12M, along with 5%, 10%, and 15% drawdown hit rates.
Validation StandardHigh-risk deciles should show deeper forward max drawdowns than low-risk deciles. If that relationship fails, the score should be treated as descriptive or redesigned.

Optimized Base Weights

The allocation model starts from backtested production base weights, then adjusts them with the weekly signal stack. The optimization used weekly equal-weight ETF group returns, PM-style sleeve constraints, and a Sharpe/Calmar/drawdown objective so the base is diversified rather than simply chasing the highest-return sleeve.

Backtest Window2021 through current price history
Base RoleStrategic starting policy before weekly overlays
Weekly AdjustmentsGroup Strategy Score, z-score overlay, FCI, CFTC positioning, VAMS, and regime tilt
Final StepWeights are normalized after score and regime tilts

Drawdown Risk Predictive Validation

This table is the institutional check on the drawdown gauge. It compares low-risk deciles 1-3 against high-risk deciles 8-10. The model is considered useful when high-risk buckets produce deeper future SPY max drawdowns and higher drawdown hit rates.

The right side of the table is the forward drawdown test. Low-Risk / High-Risk Avg Max DD compare average future max drawdowns; Extra Avg DD Risk is normalized so positive means high-risk readings led to deeper average drawdowns. Worst Max DD is the deepest observed future drawdown in each bucket. The >5%, >10%, and >15% DD Hit columns show the share of observations that later crossed those drawdown thresholds. Extra 10% Hit Risk is normalized so positive means high-risk readings were followed by more frequent 10% drawdowns.

Portfolio Regime

Current regime: Cut Risk And Wait For Repair. Internal damage or weak trend participation argues for beta restraint. The priority is drawdown control until breadth repair is visible. ETF z-scores show 16 washed-out ETFs, so repair candidates matter more than chasing current winners.

Regime Decision Framework

Portfolio StateWhat Has To Be TruePM Action
Add Broad Equity RiskIndexes and sectors are both healthy; damage breadth is contained.Own broad beta, reduce cash drag, and add to confirmed leaders.
Own Growth, Do Not Chase The Whole MarketTech/growth is strong, but sector breadth is not broad enough.Keep exposure concentrated in confirmed growth leadership; avoid broad-market overconfidence.
Favor Cyclicals And Economic BetaCyclicals lead, defensives lag, and damage remains controlled.Favor discretionary, financials, industrials, materials, housing, and infrastructure if credit confirms.
Get DefensiveDefensive sectors lead while cyclicals lag.Cut cyclical beta; prefer quality, staples, health care, utilities, real estate, or cash.
Participate, But Keep Quality BiasBroad beta is usable and rates/credit are stable, but breadth is not strong enough for maximum risk.Participate through higher-quality equity, duration, and credit expressions; avoid weak beta chase.
Favor Real Assets / Inflation HedgesCommodity and real-asset groups lead while growth weakens.Shift incremental risk toward energy, materials, metals, commodities, or inflation hedges.
Cut Risk And Wait For RepairDamage breadth is high or fewer ETFs remain in intermediate uptrends.Raise quality, reduce beta, use cash, and wait for breadth repair before adding risk.
Selective OnlySignals are strong in pockets but uneven across the whole map.Use group diagnostics and VAMS confirmation to choose exposures one sleeve at a time.

Actionable Positioning Playbook

SetupSignalAction
Crowded long + price/breadth confirmationHigh positioning percentile, positive 13W price, and supportive breadth.Maintain exposure, but add only on clean pullbacks or fresh breadth expansion.
Crowded long + positioning fadingPrice rises while institutional/HF positioning rolls over.Treat as narrowing sponsorship; reduce chase risk and watch for reversal.
Crowded short + price stabilizationLow positioning percentile while price and/or breadth stop deteriorating.Add to repair watchlist; squeeze risk can be favorable if macro backdrop confirms.
Large WoW positioning addOne-week institutional/HF flow is one of the largest in the table.Check whether this is confirmation of a trend or late crowding into an extended move.
Large WoW positioning cutOne-week institutional/HF selling is concentrated in an asset.Use as a risk warning when price is also weak; use as contrarian fuel only if price holds.

Crowded long + strong breadthPrice trend, ETF health, and CFTC positioning all agree.Maintain exposure, but avoid chasing if weekly breadth momentum fades.

Neutral positioning + improving pricePrice and breadth improve before the crowd has fully moved in.Cleaner entry setup if rates/credit are not deteriorating.

Model Allocation

A signal-driven model allocation based on optimized base weights, group scores, regime, financial-conditions risk budget, CFTC equity-crowding overlay, and the full VAMS buy/sell universe plus fresh flip momentum overlay. It is a strategy translation layer, not a position-sizing recommendation. Price/breadth as of 2026-06-05; breadth metrics as of 2026-06-05; CFTC positioning as of 2026-06-02; VAMS as of 2026-06-10.

Interpretation: Base Weight is the backtested production anchor. Signal is the base group score after breadth, price returns, trend, damage, and ETF-deck z-score extension/repair overlay. Positioning, VAMS, and FCI overlays adjust the signal where each input is relevant to the sleeve. Adjusted Signal drives Score Tilt; Regime Tilt then applies the current top-down regime before final model weights are normalized. The sleeves are intentionally broad enough to frame a portfolio, but detailed enough that style, factor, thematic, sector, industry, international, rates/credit, metals, commodities, and cash decisions do not collapse into the same repeated message.
